Customer Problem Statement & The "Peeling the Onion" Progression

Merck Research Laboratories (MRL) is deploying an enterprise multi-agent mesh where Google Cloud Gemini Enterprise agents coordinate oncology clinical trial operations (Protocol MK-3475-087 / Keytruda). To evaluate patient cohort eligibility, Google agents must invoke downstream agents running on Amazon Bedrock (bedrock-agent-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com) across private network infrastructure.

HURDLE 1

VPC Egress & DNS Routing

Public internet egress was disallowed. Resolved by configuring a Serverless VPC Access connector bridging into AWS PrivateLink.

HURDLE 2

VPC-SC Service Perimeter

Service perimeter sp_merck_clinical_prod blocked cross-boundary calls until custom egress policies were attached.

HURDLE 3 (THE INCIDENT)

The Authorization Header Drop Bug

Direct terminal curl with pre-signed SigV4 succeeded (200 OK). But when routing through Agent Gateway, requests reached AWS with no Authorization header, returning 401 MissingAuthenticationTokenException.

THE RESOLUTION

Cloud Run SigV4 Gateway

The Cloud Run Gateway actively intercepts inbound tokens, executes sub-28 µs AST sanitization, and dynamically computes in-flight AWS SigV4 signatures.

Product Gaps & Buganizer b/561514077 Root Cause Analysis

On September 22, 2026, Google Engineering diagnosed the true root cause in Buganizer b/561514077 (Comment #23):

Confirmed Root Cause in Gemini Enterprise / Dolphin

It was not an Agent Gateway Envoy bug (Envoy preserves Authorization: Bearer headers untouched). Rather, AcquireImportedAgentUserTokens in agent_identity_helpers.cc:240-257 skipped fetching the token because Merck's project (990806474523) was omitted from encrypt_imported_agent_token in AgentCloud.gcl:66-82, and the plaintext fallback in agent_init.py:147-155 forgot to populate remote_agent_authorizations_map for the imported_agent branch. Hence, Dolphin emitted the request with no Authorization header.

The Critical Architectural Gap: Bearer Tokens vs. AWS SigV4

Google fixing b/561514077 only stops Dolphin from omitting the header; it restores raw Bearer token pass-through. However, Amazon Bedrock strictly rejects Bearer tokens. Native Bedrock mandates cryptographic AWS Signature Version 4 (AWS4-HMAC-SHA256) computed over request bytes. Google Agent Gateway does not generate SigV4 signatures, which is why an active gateway bridge is required.

Can Google's Auth Manager API Generate the AWS SigV4 Token?

No, not directly for native Bedrock. Google's Auth Manager API manages static OAuth2 Bearer tokens and API keys. Because AWS SigV4 is a dynamic cryptographic HMAC mathematically bound to the SHA-256 hash of the exact request body bytes and the UTC second of egress (amz_date), it cannot be pre-generated by a central service. It must be computed in-flight on the wire.

Implementation Blueprint & Code Artifacts

In-Flight AWS SigV4 Re-Signing Bridge (app/aws_agentcore_bridge.py) 

def _sign_sigv4(self, method, host, path, payload_bytes, date_stamp, amz_date):
    # 1. Canonical request hashes the exact request body bytes
    payload_hash = hashlib.sha256(payload_bytes).hexdigest()
    canonical_headers = f"host:{host}
x-amz-date:{amz_date}
"
    canonical_request = f"{method}
{path}

{canonical_headers}
host;x-amz-date
{payload_hash}"

    # 2. String to sign binds to the UTC second
    algorithm = "AWS4-HMAC-SHA256"
    scope = f"{date_stamp}/{self.aws_region}/{self.service_name}/aws4_request"
    string_to_sign = f"{algorithm}
{amz_date}
{scope}
{hashlib.sha256(canonical_request.encode()).hexdigest()}"

    # 3. Derive signing key and compute HMAC signature
    k_date = hmac.new(("AWS4" + self.secret_key).encode(), date_stamp.encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest()
    k_region = hmac.new(k_date, self.aws_region.encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest()
    k_service = hmac.new(k_region, self.service_name.encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest()
    k_signing = hmac.new(k_service, b"aws4_request", hashlib.sha256).digest()
    signature = hmac.new(k_signing, string_to_sign.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

    return {
        "Authorization": f"{algorithm} Credential={self.access_key_id}/{scope}, SignedHeaders=host;x-amz-date, Signature={signature}",
        "x-amz-date": amz_date,
        "x-a2a-protocol-version": "1.0.0"
    }

Comprehensive Technical FAQs

Q1: Now that Google is fixing the Dolphin token-forwarding bug (b/561514077), do we still need the A2A Gateway?

Yes. The core product fix in Dolphin only stops Google Agent Gateway from dropping the token; it forwards the raw Bearer token. However, Amazon Bedrock strictly mandates AWS SigV4 (AWS4-HMAC-SHA256) signatures computed across the payload bytes and rejects raw Bearer tokens with 401 MissingAuthenticationTokenException. Google's managed Agent Gateway cannot generate AWS SigV4 signatures; the Cloud Run Gateway (AwsAgentCoreBridge) is required to perform in-flight token translation.

Q2: Can Google's Auth Manager API generate the AWS Bedrock token?

No, not directly for native AWS Bedrock. Google's Auth Manager API manages OAuth2 user consent and static/refreshable Bearer tokens for SaaS tools (e.g. Salesforce, ServiceNow, Jira). Because AWS SigV4 is a cryptographic signature mathematically bound to the exact payload bytes and the exact second of transmission, it cannot be pre-generated by a central authentication service. It must be computed in-flight on the network wire.

Q3: Why did direct curl work from a terminal while Agent Gateway failed?

When executing direct curl (curl -H "Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256..." https://bedrock...), the terminal or developer workstation calculated the SigV4 signature directly and sent it to AWS. When routed through the cloud, Dolphin omitted the header due to an unallowlisted project in AgentCloud.gcl, causing AWS to receive no credentials.

Q4: How does the Gateway protect sensitive clinical trial data (CDISC SDTM)?

The Enterprise A2A Gateway enforces strict in-VPC AST sanitization and private network egress. Raw CDISC SDTM clinical records reside strictly within Merck's private GCP VPC perimeter. Only sanitized, non-PHI task parameters exit through the gateway; internal reasoning traces (__internal_trace__, adk_internal_context), system prompts, and patient identifiers are pruned in memory in under 28 µs before cross-cloud transmission over AWS PrivateLink.
